story.error_policy: Supportive spoken feedback over current still, optional subtle UI cue, preserve evidence and allow retry. No extra video required. No humiliating failure or punitive countdown.
story.audio_policy: Use one recorded line at a time. Branch lines play only when their explicit condition is triggered. Never sort the entire directory alphabetically and play it as one story.
story.video_policy: Six separate MP4s, each <= 5.0 seconds. No looping for longer speech; hold end frame while the recording continues. Use provided END keyframe as a deterministic fallback.

questions.prompt: In the metallic bonding model, what happens to the valence electrons?

options.B: They become delocalized throughout the metallic structure.
options.C: They form a separate set of negative metal ions.
options.D: Each electron is fixed between only two neighbouring cores.

questions.explanation: Valence electrons are delocalized through the metallic structure; they remain part of the material.

questions.prompt: Which attraction holds a metallic structure together?

options.A: Attraction between two positive metal ion cores alone.
options.B: Attraction between negative metal ions and neutral atoms.
options.C: Attraction between different nuclei after protons transfer.
options.D: Electrostatic attraction between positive metal ion cores and delocalized electrons.

questions.explanation: The positive cores and delocalized negative electrons are the charged components in this model.

questions.prompt: A sodium atom transfers one electron to a chlorine atom. Which result is correct?

options.A: Na+ and Cl- form; their proton counts stay the same.
options.B: Na- and Cl+ form; their proton counts stay the same.
options.D: The elements change because their nuclei exchange protons.

questions.explanation: Sodium loses an electron and becomes positive; chlorine gains it and becomes negative. Their nuclei do not change.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly separates electron transfer from ionic bonding in the sodium-chlorine model?

options.A: The transfer itself is the only force keeping the completed solid together.
options.B: Electron transfer makes neutral atoms that then share an electron sea.
options.C: Transfer produces ions; electrostatic attraction between opposite ions is ionic bonding.
options.D: Transfer removes all electrons from both atoms.

questions.explanation: Forming charged ions and explaining the force between those ions are related but distinct steps.

questions.prompt: Model X contains positive metal ion cores and delocalized electrons. Model Y contains repeating cations and anions. Which comparison is correct?

options.A: Both are ionic structures because both contain positive particles.
options.B: X is metallic and Y is ionic; both involve electrostatic attraction between different charged components.
options.C: X is ionic and Y is metallic.
options.D: Both are metallic because all solids have an electron sea.

questions.explanation: The particles involved and their arrangement distinguish the metallic and ionic models, not their illustration colours.
